seo.metaTitle: PNG to Base64 - Free Encoder, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Encode a PNG as a Base64 string in your browser and copy it into CSS, HTML or JSON. No upload, no account, no limits, and the data never leaves the page.
seo.longDescription: Base64 is the text encoding that turns binary image data into a string safe to paste into source code: a CSS background, an HTML attribute, a JSON config or an email template. Encoding a PNG here produces that string in the result panel, with a button to copy it to the clipboard. The image is read in your browser and encoded there, so the picture and the resulting data never leave your device - which matters because a Base64 string is the image itself, and uploading it would be uploading your file. The result can be used as a data URI directly.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Wait for the string to appear in the result panel.
Press the copy button to put the whole string on the clipboard.
Use it in CSS as url(data:image/png;base64,...) or paste it where you need.

faq.q: Why is the string longer than the file?
faq.a: Base64 stores six bits per character, so it costs about 33 percent more characters than the raw bytes: a 300 KB PNG becomes roughly 400 KB of text. It is a transport format, not a compression one.

faq.q: Should I embed images as Base64?
faq.a: For small assets - icons, sprites, logos, a few kilobytes - yes, it removes a request and guarantees the image travels with the file. For photos and anything large it usually hurts: the text is bigger, it cannot be cached separately and it blocks parsing.

faq.q: Is the string the whole image?
faq.a: Yes, which is why this page never uploads anything. A Base64 string of your picture is as sensitive as the picture itself, so keep it on your machine.

faq.q: What is the difference between Base64 and a data URI?
faq.a: A data URI is the full string you put in an attribute: the prefix with the MIME type, then the Base64 payload. Copy the data URI variant when you need the ready-made value for src or background-image.
